subject: Post-demo pricing workback & caching assumptions
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@finova.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — follow-up on pricing targets and usage

Marcus — thanks for the demo today. Good conversation; a couple quick follow-ups so we can see whether this maps to our budget.

High level usage (approx):
- Monthly tokens (combined prompts + completions): ~75M tokens
- Typical average sequence length: 220 tokens
- Peak query rate: ~5 qps (short spikes to 8 qps)
- Expected growth: +25% over 6 months if early pilot succeeds

Budget band (what procurement has): $40k–$60k / month.

Key asks for your team:
1) Work backward to a target effective $/1M tokens that would let us sit in that band given the 75M tokens a month profile.
2) Show 2–3 caching/hit-rate scenarios and how they change the effective $/1M tokens (Elena: we use lots of repeated prompts, so prefix caching could be meaningful).
3) Any assumptions you need from us (prompt mix, percent of short vs long completions).

I've attached a small sample of anonymized usage (CSV). Procurement is on copy for the pricing band.

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of AI Products, Finova
elena@finova.com

On Tue, Feb 24, 2027 at 3:12 PM Elena Torres <elena@finova.com> wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the demo today. Good conversation; a couple quick follow-ups so we can see whether this maps to our budget.

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the sample usage. Quick working-back exercise below; I looped in Laura and Ben for pricing/ops input.

Summary (ballpark, initial assumptions):
- Model baseline list price we would use for quoting (open/recommended): $480 / 1M tokens
- Cacheable prefix portion assumption: 40% (this is our mid-case — depends on prompt overlap)
- Effective price formula used: effective = baseline * (1 - hit_rate) + cached_cost * hit_rate. For prefix cache we treat cached_cost near $0 incremental (served from mem/fast store).

Working examples for 1M tokens:
- No caching (0% hit): $480 / 1M
- Mid-case (40% prefix hit): $480 * (1 - 0.40) = $288 / 1M
- Aggressive (55% prefix hit): $480 * (1 - 0.55) = $216 / 1M
- Conservative (30% prefix hit): $480 * (1 - 0.30) = $336 / 1M

Mapping to your 75M tokens / month: (rounded)
- No cache: 75 * $480 = $36,000 / month
- Mid-case (40%): 75 * $288 = $21,600 / month
- Aggressive (55%): 75 * $216 = $16,200 / month
- Conservative (30%): 75 * $336 = $25,200 / month

Observation: With a 40%+ prefix hit we land inside or just below your procurement band once you account for lane-specific costs (support, any private deployment add-ons). Without caching you'd be slightly below the $40k floor in this example — procurement's band likely assumes additional seat/support / integration costs.

Assumptions / caveats:
- Baseline $480/1M is list-reference for the model we demoed; alternative model variants/quantization move the baseline down ~15–30%.
- Cache effectiveness heavily depends on prompt reuse and where the reuse occurs (prefixes vs full messages).
- We treat cached responses as near-zero marginal cost here; in practice Redis/edge store and extra band-width/ops have a small cost we can include in final quote (~$5–$25 / 1M tokens range depending on footprint).

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura/Ben: run 3 formal scenarios (conservative/mid/aggressive) with a line-item for infra/ops and provide a deck.
2) Elena: if possible, share a short prompt-mix (percent short <100 tokens vs >300 tokens) or confirm whether the sample is representative. That will let us refine hit-rate projections.
3) I'll send a first Mutual Action Plan (attached) and propose an initial 6-week pilot pricing and SLA (pilot discounted, predictable capacity).

I'll follow up tomorrow with the scenario table from Laura.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2027 08:05:00 -0800

Marcus — quick internal notes before we send Elena the scenario table: 

Pricing ops checklist / adjustments:
- Hit-rate range: recommend using 30% / 45% / 60% for conservative/mid/aggressive buckets. Many customers reporting high prefix reuse see 50–60% after initial prompt engineering.
- Baseline model variants: include a quantized v2 at -20% baseline and a smaller nearby model at -35% baseline. That gives the buyer more cost-perf choices.
- Infra adders: include a separate line for dedicated pool capacity (if they want predictable throughput) — this is typically a monthly committed uplift, not token-based.
- Small per-1M ops overhead (we should model $12 / 1M for cache infra + monitoring traces in this example).

I'll prepare a 1-page table showing per-1M effective price and total month cost for the three hit-rate scenarios at the three baseline variants (list / quantized / small-model). Ben, please confirm the dedicated pool uplift numbers (I put placeholders).

Laura
Laura Bennett
Pricing & Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finova.com>, Finova Procurement <procurement@finova.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Consolidated numbers + next steps (pilot & MPA)

Elena — looping back with the refined guidance from our ops team and an attached MPA. TL;DR numbers are below; full breakdown is attached (Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.docx) and I posted the scenario spreadsheet here: https://drive.google.com/finova/cache-analysis

Refined effective $/1M (examples) — baseline = $480 / 1M, + $12 / 1M infra adder:
- Conservative (30% prefix hit): $480*(1-0.30) + $12 = $348 / 1M
- Mid (45% prefix hit): $480*(1-0.45) + $12 = $270 / 1M
- Aggressive (60% prefix hit): $480*(1-0.60) + $12 = $204 / 1M

Mapped to 75M tokens / month (rounded):
- Conservative: 75 * $348 = $26,100 / month
- Mid: 75 * $270 = $20,250 / month
- Aggressive: 75 * $204 = $15,300 / month

How this fits your $40k–$60k band: those procurement numbers likely include dedicated capacity and premium support. If Finova wants a predictable Dedicated pool we can model a committed uplift (example: +$20k / month for reserved GPU capacity sized for 5 qps sustained with burst headroom). Combining a mid-case token spend + a modest dedicated uplift is what typically lands in an enterprise procurement band.

Ask / next steps:
- Elena: confirm the sample coverage or share an anonymized prompt-mix (short vs long). That will let us pick the right hit-rate bucket.
- Procurement: if you expect Dedicated (reserved) capacity, say so and we'll include a committed uplift in the MPA.
- Proposed next call: 30-minute pricing walk-through (we'll bring engineering to talk SLO/latency impact of caching) — are you available next Tue 2/2 or Wed 2/3 in the morning PST?

If you want, we can also start a 6-week pilot at the mid-case rates with an explicit checkpoint to validate hit-rate and then true-up pricing.

Thanks —
Marcus
